items.text: Kambiz Tavana said the Iran issue could become part of broader Washington-Beijing talks on topics like Taiwan and North Korea. Iran's position, especially with China's role in oil purchases and Strait of Hormuz developments, affects Tehran's bargaining power. The main priority of both countries remains economic issues and trade competition, with regional topics discussed within this framework.

Netanyahu stated that the rulers of Tehran fear the Iranian people more than anything else. These remarks were made in the audio version of program 24 with Fardad Farahzad. The topic relates to political concerns in Iran.

Danny Danon, Israel's ambassador to the UN, offered a Starlink satellite internet device to Iranian diplomat Nasser Asadi at the UN General Assembly. Asadi did not accept or acknowledge the device. The device had been previously introduced by Benjamin Netanyahu to help Iranians bypass internet censorship.

Turkey and Iraq agreed on the gradual transfer of the Bashiqa military base to the Iraqi government after their leaders met in New York. This base has been a major point of dispute for over a decade. They also emphasized the return of Iraqi sovereignty over the Sinjar region and the end of illegal foreign armed groups there.

The Kuwaiti Crown Prince accused the Islamic Republic of carrying out missile and drone attacks against Kuwait and GCC countries as well as Jordan. He described these attacks as violations of international law and the UN Charter, targeting civilian infrastructure. He also accused Iran of disrupting shipping and using the Strait of Hormuz as a bargaining tool.

Abdullah Abdulqadir Al-Alimi, deputy head of Yemen's leadership council, accused the Houthis of rejecting the Saudi and Omani peace roadmap and escalating tensions in the Red Sea and Bab al-Mandab to serve Iran's goals. He said these actions have turned one of the world's most important waterways into a tool of pressure. He also emphasized that protecting Bab al-Mandab is a shared regional and international responsibility.

Luis Montenegro, the Prime Minister of Portugal, condemned the actions of the Iranian government and its affiliated groups in his speech at the United Nations. He called for an end to attacks on neighboring countries, commercial ships, and civilian facilities, as well as the lifting of the blockade of the Strait of Hormuz. He also described the protection of seas and freedom of navigation as a shared responsibility requiring collective cooperation.

Masoud Pezeshkian stated that everyone in Iran has the right to protest but described the December protests as a coup attempt. He announced the death toll as three thousand and apologized for mismanagement. He also said that the instructions come from Mojtaba Khamenei and the government implements them.

Colombia announced it has cut diplomatic relations with the Islamic Republic of Iran as of September 19, 2026. The reasons include security concerns, alleged ties between Tehran and terrorist groups, human rights violations, and Iran's actions in the region. Consular relations between the two countries will continue.

The "NIAC" group has sued US President Donald Trump for continuing the war with the Iranian government without congressional authorization. The group has asked the federal court to declare this action unconstitutional. NIAC states that the authority to declare war under the US Constitution rests with Congress, and Trump has continued the war with Iran without obtaining such authorization.

About 80 countries issued a joint statement calling for the immediate and full reopening of the Strait of Hormuz and condemned attacks by Iran and the Houthis. The statement was read by Bahrain's foreign minister at the United Nations. The signatories emphasized the safe passage of ships through this waterway.

Saudi Arabia, Turkey, and Pakistan will hold an emergency meeting with their military commanders to discuss support for Riyadh following attacks by Yemen's Houthis. The meeting aims to review support for Riyadh's right to self-defense within the framework of a joint defense agreement. Analysts have expressed doubts about the implementation and commitment levels of the Makkah Pact.

Israeli officials believe that resuming attacks on Iran is only a matter of time and Israel is prepared defensively and offensively. They threatened to attack nuclear facilities if Tehran crosses red lines. Additionally, Israeli elections will not affect the decision for a possible attack, and the ongoing US-Iran negotiations are considered insignificant.

Masoud Pezeshkian told Fox News that Iran has never sought nuclear weapons and adheres to the framework of the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty. Responding to a question about 60% uranium enrichment, he stated that Iran is ready to dilute these materials and attributes the problem to US behavior. Pezeshkian also emphasized that Iran will continue to resist despite economic problems caused by sanctions and will not surrender.

Abbas Araghchi stated that Iran has made a proposal to the US that could lead to the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz and the resumption of negotiations for a final agreement. The proposal was presented to Washington through intermediaries, and the US must implement specific conditions within seven days. The details of the conditions were not disclosed but are said to be more than the terms of the Islamabad agreement.

Dani Danon, Israel's ambassador to the UN, offered Naser Asadi, the representative of the Islamic Republic, a Starlink device in a video and suggested he take it to Tehran. He said the device could be useful in Iran and help the Iranian people achieve freedom. Danon also expressed hope for regime change in Iran.

The Russian Foreign Ministry announced that Sergey Lavrov and Abbas Araghchi emphasized the necessity of a diplomatic resolution to the crisis caused by the US and Israel's war against Iran during their meeting in New York. The ministry called the actions of the US and Israel illegal and stated there is no alternative to a diplomatic solution. Russia and Iran signed a strategic partnership agreement in 2025 that foresees closer defense cooperation.

Masoud Pezeshkian has expressed readiness to inspect nuclear facilities and address the issue of 60% uranium reserves. He and Abbas Araghchi tried to show in New York that the Islamic Republic is ready for agreement and cooperation. Pezeshkian did not give a clear answer about guaranteeing military forces' adherence to the potential agreement.

Mohammad Motamedizadeh, a member of the Presidium of the Parliament's Article 90 Commission, announced in an interview with the Khaneh Mellat news agency on Friday, the 3rd of Mehr that if US threats continue, withdrawing from the Non-Proliferation Treaty (NPT) could be put on the agenda. He described these threats as a sign of the other side's desperation. He also emphasized that one should not show weakness in the face of threats.

The Islamic Republic has proposed reopening the Strait of Hormuz in exchange for reducing or lifting the naval blockade. Kamyar Behrang says this waterway is no longer an effective leverage in negotiations with the US. The Strait of Hormuz issue has become a global crisis, with pressure from various countries to reopen it.

Shayan Samiei stated that the Houthi attacks on Saudi oil export routes aim to prevent Saudi Arabia from using an alternative safe route. These attacks increase risk, insurance costs, and ship rental fees. The Houthis want to increase pressure on Saudi Arabia regarding finding an alternative oil export route.

Fatemeh Mohitizadeh, Iran's heptathlon representative at the Nagoya Asian Games, was disqualified for wearing non-standard shoes after competing in six events and holding second place overall. Only one event remained, and she likely could have medaled. She had achieved top ranks in several events including the 100-meter hurdles and high jump.

Hanieh Rostamian and Vahid Golkhandan won the bronze medal in the mixed pistol event at the Nagoya Asian Games with 415 points. The Indian team took first place with 484 points, and South Korea came second with 478 points.

Mehdi Saremi Far emphasized the importance of free internet and Starlink for the people of Iran. He stated that the Islamic Republic has used communication shutdowns as a tool for repression. Starlink cannot fully replace Iran's internet but helps people maintain their connections.

Masoud Pezeshkian held a meeting on the evening of October 2 in New York with several prominent figures in American media and think tanks. Attendees included Robert Malley and Trita Parsi. The meeting took place on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly.

The management of Najaf Airport announced the suspension of all incoming flights from Iran and outgoing flights to Iran from 2 AM Friday until further notice. This decision was made based on official orders from relevant authorities. The Iranian Civil Aviation Organization also announced the suspension of accepting flights of Iranian airlines at Baghdad Airport.

On the third day of the 81st United Nations General Assembly, Benjamin Netanyahu emphasized the collapse of the Islamic Republic of Iran. He stated that the ruling regime in Iran fears its people more than anything else. This report was provided by Ashkan Safaei from Iran International.

Abbas Araghchi stated in a meeting with the Portuguese foreign minister that insecurity in the Strait of Hormuz is a result of actions by the US and Israel. He called for stopping unsafe actions by the US to restore maritime security. He also urged the European Union to adopt an independent and responsible approach to regional developments.

Hossein Abdi resigned as head coach of Iran's U23 football team after returning to Iran. The team was eliminated in the group stage of the 2026 Asian Games in Nagoya. Abdi accepted responsibility for the results and apologized to the Iranian people.

A court session was held for nine women residing in Ahvaz at the Revolutionary Court of the city. They are accused of membership in opposition groups, propaganda against the regime, and conspiracy against internal or external security. The judge sentenced each to five years in prison, with a reduction to one year if they complete a mandatory ideological reform period.

Iranians in Germany held a rally on Friday, September 25, in support of Ali Zarei in front of the US Embassy in Dusseldorf. Ali Zarei is a protester of the Mahsa movement and a prisoner in Iran facing the risk of execution. The demonstrators demanded action to prevent his execution.

The police commander of Yazd province announced the arrest of a woman in the province. She is accused of involvement in the arson of a mosque in Tehran and disturbing public order during last December's protests. This information was reported by Harana News Agency.

Morteza Nemati, the Nagoya Asian Games champion, admitted to pretending to have a mental disorder to get a military exemption. He said after returning to Iran that he obtained a psychiatric exemption in the past year. Nemati did this to participate in national team camps and acknowledges that his action was wrong.

A citizen reported in a video that water was continuously cut off for 33 hours. Due to the depletion of water reserves, he faced difficulties in bathing and cleaning his shop. The citizen addressed Masoud Pezeshkian and asked if the United States had cut the water.

A viewer of Iran International said Masoud Pezeshkian's speech does not matter to them, and they consider the speeches of Donald Trump and Benjamin Netanyahu more important. The viewer identified Reza Pahlavi as the true representative of the Iranian people. They hope Reza Pahlavi will attend international assemblies as the official representative of the Iranian nation.

Hamid Ghaeni-Nejad, a resident of Mashhad, remains in indefinite detention in Vakilabad prison after six months. He suffers from physical problems and requires continuous medical care but has been deprived of proper treatment. Forensic medicine has confirmed his inability to endure imprisonment, and a one billion toman bail has been set, which he cannot afford.

A citizen in Shiraz spray-painted an image of Mohammad Reza Shah Pahlavi on a wall. Next to the image, a famous verse from Shahnameh and slogans "Long live Iran" and "Long live the Shah" were written. This video was published by Iran International.

Rouhollah Rahimpour spoke about China's role in Tehran-Washington negotiations, stating that Beijing can play a significant mediating role. He added that this role cannot be considered decisive. China has relations and economic interests with both sides.

Mohsen Mahyemini from Iran International said many viewers considered Benjamin Netanyahu the voice of the Iranian people in the world after his speech. Some viewers also hope that Prince Reza Pahlavi will attend next year's General Assembly meeting.

Iranian representatives won silver and bronze medals in gymnastics, rowing, and shooting at the Asian Games. Fatemeh Mohitizadeh was disqualified from athletics for using unauthorized shoes. More details were reported by Alireza Modiri.

The Iranian men's 3x3 basketball team defeated the Philippines 21-10 in the bronze medal match at the Nagoya Asian Games. The players included Mohammad Ghaffari, Basir Momeni, Sarem Jafari, and Mohammad-Mehdi Rahimi. Iran lost 14-11 to Qatar in the semifinals.

Security forces used live ammunition, shotguns, and deadly weapons to suppress protests in Kurdistan, Kermanshah, and West Azerbaijan. These actions have been reported in these regions. Protests continue in these provinces.

Amir Safari's family and children held a birthday ceremony at his grave in Behesht Zahra on the first of Mehr. A dove was released in memory of him during the ceremony. Amir Safari was killed on January 9, 2026, in the Sattarkhan neighborhood of Tehran at the age of 48.

The Left Party of Germany, after winning the Berlin elections, intends to invite the Green Party and the Social Democrats to preliminary coalition talks. The Green and Social Democratic parties have conditioned the start of negotiations on an agreement to protect the lives of Jewish citizens. The Left Party will vote on the official invitation at its congress.

Donald Trump and Xi Jinping emphasized maintaining stability and expanding cooperation. Despite disagreements on issues like trade and Taiwan, the two countries must interact. China prefers to play a mediating role regarding the Islamic Republic.

The Iranian U23 football team returned to Tehran after a 4-1 loss to North Korea and elimination from the group stage of the Nagoya Asian Games. Esmaeil Gholizadeh apologized to the public and cited infrastructure issues and last-minute player additions as reasons for the defeat. He denied rumors of player negligence and expressed hope for the future.

Saeed Shirali, 22 years old, was killed on the evening of January 8 during protests on Azadi Street in Tehran by government forces. His mother said she searched for him for three days and found his body with three bullet wounds.

Families of political prisoners executed in 1988 were prevented from entering Khavaran Cemetery today and placed their flowers behind closed gates. They held a ceremony at the site to honor the victims. Security forces filmed the families at the end of the ceremony.

Mohammad Mokhber reacted to the suspension of Iranian airlines' flights in some countries and threatened those countries. He stated that flights in the region should be free for everyone or for no one. He also said that if Iran cannot fly or receive airport services, no country in the region will have this possibility either.

Amnesty International launched a global campaign to end impunity for perpetrators of crimes against humanity in Iran, coinciding with the release of a report on the crackdown on the Woman, Life, Freedom uprising. The organization has called on people to sign a petition urging UN member states to establish an international mechanism to investigate and prosecute those responsible.

Iran's men's and women's national kabaddi teams advanced to the final of the Nagoya Asian Games by winning their semifinals. The women's team defeated Taiwan 23-19, and the men's team won 59-21. Both teams will face India in the final.

Mohammad Saeedi called unveiling hijab religiously and politically forbidden and demanded action against women who do not observe hijab. He emphasized that those unaware should be dealt with through education and awareness. He also stated that those who deliberately threaten national security must face legal and security measures.

The Italian Council of Ministers approved a plan to ban the burqa, masks, and face-covering garments that prevent full identification of students in schools. Violations of these regulations will be fined up to one thousand euros. This news was reported by Sadaf Baghbani.

In Bojnord, mosques and Hosseiniyehs were used to deploy forces and organize plainclothes agents. One Hosseiniyeh was turned into a gathering place for plainclothes forces. Surveillance cameras were also used to identify protesters.

The Israeli Prime Minister accused Recep Tayyip Erdogan of being responsible for the killing of thousands of Kurdish civilians at the UN General Assembly. He also criticized the Turkish government for suppressing the Kurds. These statements were made in Benjamin Netanyahu's speech.

Pezhman Amani from Saqez and Shahin Mostafazadeh from Mahabad were arrested separately by intelligence agents on Wednesday, 1 Mehr. They were transferred to an unknown location. Pezhman Amani's and his family members' phones were also confiscated.

The Amitt Institute for Terrorism and Intelligence Research reported an increase in the role of Chinese parts in the Houthi's military capabilities. The institute stated that China has become one of the main sources for supplying drone parts and weapons to the Houthis. This report is based on data from intercepted shipments.
The Australian national team scored first in the 68th minute with a goal by Nestori Iranconda. Brazil equalized in the 90+5th minute with a goal by Ryan. The match ended in a draw.

Ali Hossein Ghazizadeh stated that regional countries previously sought an agreement to permanently limit Iran's nuclear and missile threats. He added that with increased US sanctions and naval and air blockades, the situation has changed. Regional countries now prefer to continue pressure until Iran accepts the conditions of the US and the region.

Pakistan's Foreign Ministry announced that under the Makkah joint defense agreement, an attack on any member is considered an attack on all members. The foreign ministers of the three countries met on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly and condemned attacks on Saudi Arabia. They also discussed holding an urgent meeting of military chiefs and establishing the agreement's secretariat.

Benjamin Netanyahu's plane passed through Canadian airspace en route to New York for a UN General Assembly speech. Canada had previously stated it would enforce the ICC arrest warrant if Netanyahu entered its territory. A Canadian foreign ministry spokesperson said the overflight permission does not imply endorsement of Israeli policies and was granted due to the importance of diplomatic interactions.

With new US sanctions against Iran's aviation industry, flight restrictions for Iranian companies in the region have increased. Flights from Iran to Najaf, Erbil, and Sulaymaniyah have been stopped. Access to other routes has also faced limitations.

The mother of Amir Setarirad participated in the memorial campaign by lighting a candle at his grave. Amir Setarirad was an environmental researcher and teacher who was killed on January 9, 2026, in Karaj. His mother expressed the absence of her son in the classroom.

Masoud Pezeshkian rejected the published statistics about the casualties of the December protests in an interview with Fox News. He stated that the number of casualties was slightly more than three thousand. These remarks were made in an interview with Samira Gharaei, a reporter for Iran International.

Two emergency medical experts in Shiraz were attacked with a cold weapon by individuals under the influence of drugs and alcohol during a mission. One expert has been discharged from the hospital, while the other underwent surgery due to lung injury. The condition of the second expert is reported as stable.

David Perdue, the US ambassador to China, stated that Trump told Xi Jinping that any direct or indirect Chinese support to Iran is unacceptable. Washington is concerned about indirect Chinese support for Iran but lacks direct evidence. Trump and Xi are working on building a relationship based on trust.

At the start of the school year, images of mothers who have abandoned mandatory hijab and daughters who are still required to wear the headscarf have widely circulated on social media. Ayah Dris, a member of Iran International's editorial team, has explained these reactions.

Nawaf Salam, the Prime Minister of Lebanon, called for a new chapter in Tehran-Beirut relations during a meeting with Masoud Pezeshkian on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly. He emphasized that Lebanon does not want to become a field for regional conflicts or message exchanges. This meeting took place on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly.

Iran and Middle East war developments were key topics in the UN General Assembly speeches. Some officials emphasized stopping attacks and reopening the Strait of Hormuz. This was mentioned in reference to actions by the Islamic Republic and allied groups.

The Argentine federal judge issued a verdict for the trial in absentia of seven Iranians and one Lebanese in the AMIA bombing case. Charges include murder, injury motivated by racial hatred, and crimes against humanity. An order to freeze the assets of the accused up to 500 million dollars was also issued.

Sahar Esfandiari and Sajad Kalvani were each sentenced to 11 years in prison by the Revolutionary Court in Shiraz. Their charges include propaganda against the regime, conspiracy against internal and external security, and contact with Israel and the United States. Due to multiple charges, five years of the sentence will be enforced for each.

Tina Deljou, a women's rights activist, was granted leave from Lakaan Prison in Rasht on Saturday, September 18. The leave period is reported to be 10 days. This news was reported by Harana News Agency.

The NATO Secretary General stated that the Iranian people feel the US economic sanctions daily, but the Iranian regime does not care about their interests. He said that US pressure has weakened Iran's nuclear and missile programs. He also confirmed that the Iranian people are fed up with the regime.

The British Foreign Secretary told his Iranian counterpart that the UK will not tolerate threats from Iran-affiliated groups on its soil. Abbas Araghchi criticized the actions of the US and Israel during the meeting. The two sides discussed the war in the Middle East and the importance of reopening the Strait of Hormuz.

The President of France announced the deployment of military forces and equipment to protect Saudi Arabia's oil facilities. This move follows attacks by Yemeni Houthi militants. The forces will be sent to protect the port of Yanbu.

The airports of Erbil and Sulaymaniyah in the Kurdistan Region of Iraq have suspended flights of Iranian airplanes from October 3rd. Additionally, Najaf airport has also stopped Iranian flights from Friday morning. These decisions were made following secondary US sanctions on Iranian airlines.

The official Iraqi news agency reported the suspension of all incoming and outgoing flights to and from Iran from Najaf International Airport. The Najaf airport management announced that based on official instructions, these flights will be stopped from 2 AM Friday, 3rd of Mehr, until further notice. This action follows US sanctions on Iranian airlines and comes after the suspension of Iranian flights at Baghdad airport.

Mehdi Alfti won the silver medal in the pommel horse final at the 2026 Nagoya Asian Games. Mohammadreza Hamidi placed sixth in the horizontal bar final and retired from gymnastics championship. This report was prepared by Alireza Modiri.

Mohammad Mokhber warned that if restrictions and airport service cuts for Iranian flights continue, no country in the region will be allowed to use flight services. He emphasized that flying in the region is either free for everyone or for no one. Previously, Mohsen Rezaei had made similar threats.

Fatemeh Mohitizadeh was one event away from finishing the heptathlon at the Nagoya Asian Games. She was disqualified due to her shoes being declared non-standard. More details were provided by Iran International reporters.

Ali Al-Zaidi, the Prime Minister of Iraq, emphasized his country's support for dialogue and diplomacy to reduce tensions. He announced the government's plan to diversify oil export routes and develop energy corridors. He also stated that disarmament efforts of armed groups are progressing well.
Islam Salahi, a Sunni cleric and Friday prayer leader of Vizneh village in Talesh county, was summoned to the Special Clergy Court of Gilan province in Rasht.

Nawaf Salam, the Prime Minister of Lebanon, announced his country's solidarity with Gulf countries and Jordan against attacks by the Islamic Republic during the UN General Assembly. He emphasized that the Lebanese government seeks to monopolize weapons under the state and limit war and peace decisions to legal institutions. He also called for Israel to withdraw from all Lebanese territories to internationally recognized borders.

Christophe Mirman, head of Monaco's government, expressed solidarity with Gulf countries targeted by attacks. He stated that a comprehensive agreement on Iran's nuclear program is only possible through negotiation. Mirman also called for efforts to strengthen the ceasefire in Gaza.

Amid the Chinese president's historic visit to the US and the Israeli prime minister's emphasis on overthrowing the Islamic Republic, there are speculations about Trump's decision regarding a deal or the destruction of Iran's government. Hossein Aghaei provided an analytical view on this topic in the program "Peyvast." This issue was covered by Iran International.

Recep Tayyip Erdogan stated that Turkey has kept communication channels open with the US and the Islamic Republic to prevent escalation of conflicts. He emphasized that Turkey does not want to choose sides between East and West and continues to expand relations with various powers. Erdogan also said Turkey plays a mediating role in the Ukraine war.

On the sixth day of the 2026 Asian Games in Nagoya, the Iranian delegation won 4 medals. Mehdi Alfti won a silver medal in artistic gymnastics, and the men's 3x3 basketball team won bronze. Additionally, the men's double kayak and mixed pistol teams won bronze medals, but Fatemeh Mohitizadeh was disqualified due to non-standard shoes.

With the start of the new school year, pressures and restrictions by the government and its supporters to impose the hijab in Iran continue. Meanwhile, women continue their civil resistance. More details are provided by Seba Heydarkhani.

The teenage daughter of Mansour Bagheri distributed memorial items at the site of his killing. Mansour Bagheri, a 36-year-old worker, was killed on the evening of January 8, 2026, in Fardis. This video has been released.

In the past week, 48 illegal hunters and wood traffickers were arrested, and over 24 hectares of natural resources were affected by fire. The air quality index in 7 cities was declared unhealthy. Drought crisis, waste, and pollutants were also reported as environmental issues.

The Kuwaiti Crown Prince stated that since February, Kuwait, the Gulf countries, and Jordan have been targeted by Iranian missile and drone attacks. These attacks have damaged civilian sites and critical infrastructure, causing civilian casualties. He also accused Iran of disrupting shipping and closing the Strait of Hormuz as a pressure tool in the war.

The fourth day of the 81st UN General Assembly continues with speeches by the prime ministers of Iraq, Lebanon, Pakistan, Egypt, and the Bahraini foreign minister. The speeches focus on freedom of navigation, regional security, Middle East developments, diplomacy, and economic challenges. This report is by Maryam Rahmati from Iran International.

A US defense official told Al Jazeera that on Wednesday, 60 ships passed through the Strait of Hormuz, carrying the largest daily volume of oil since July. Yesterday, a US official also told Reuters that about 60 commercial ships passed through the Strait of Hormuz. According to the official, a total of about 22 million barrels of oil passed through this strategic maritime passage.

Nazanin Sharifian, a representative of the Yashar party, said the exit of some delegations from the UN General Assembly during Netanyahu's speech indicates Israel's difficult diplomatic situation. She emphasized that as long as the Islamic Republic is in power, the security of Israel and the region will not be ensured. Sharifian also described Masoud Pezeshkian's remarks as a distorted image of the Islamic Republic and called for Israel to cooperate with the US and regional countries.

Abbas Araghchi, Iran's foreign minister, met with Faisal bin Farhan, Saudi Arabia's foreign minister, on the sidelines of the 81st UN General Assembly. He also met with India's foreign minister and attended the ECO foreign ministers' meeting.

Ali Ashiri, 21 years old, was killed by a direct shot to the heart in Dezful on the evening of January 9, 2026. His mother joined the campaign "One Candle, One Name, One Memory" and lit a candle for her son.

An independent panel found Manchester City guilty of 114 out of 115 charges of breaching Premier League financial regulations. These allegations relate to the years 2009 to 2018, and the club's punishment has not yet been determined. Manchester City is expected to appeal the decision.

Reza Pahlavi supported Colombia's decision to cut diplomatic ties with the Islamic Republic, calling it a principled action. He thanked the people of Iran and Colombia for this stance. He also expressed hope for strong and lasting friendship between a free Iran and Colombia.

Ahmad Rahimi has been held in Vakilabad Prison in Mashhad for over six months without a judicial decision. He suffers from multiple illnesses but has been deprived of specialized medical care. His legal case remains unresolved and no court session has been held for him.

A senior Iranian official stated that even if the US accepts Iran's proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, Iran will not show any flexibility in its nuclear program. The official emphasized that the Strait of Hormuz will remain closed until all of Iran's conditions are met by the US. The proposal includes lifting the US naval blockade of Iranian ports.

Ali Al-Zaidi, the Prime Minister of Iraq, announced that after the end of the international coalition's mission in Iraq, the country's relations with strategic partners will shift to economic and developmental cooperation. He also called for increased border control and vigilance against extremism. These remarks were made at the United Nations General Assembly.

The US Central Command released images of US Marines training on the USS Boxer to enforce a naval blockade of Iran. CENTCOM has routed 122 commercial ships by October 3 to ensure strict compliance with the blockade. These exercises aim to implement the naval blockade of Iran.

A citizen reported in a video to Iran International that the water supply in their area in Tehran has been completely cut off since Friday, October 3rd. This issue has lasted at least one day. No further details were provided.

Pope Leo XIV arrived in Paris and met with Emmanuel Macron. The Vatican announced that the Pope will hold a prayer ceremony in the restored Notre-Dame Cathedral. He will also meet with victims of sexual abuse.

Donald Trump said that US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent is doing very well and will not leave his position. He also denied reports that Bessent would be appointed as the Chief Superintelligence Officer, calling them fake news, and emphasized that he does not intend to reassign him.
A 25-year-old citizen was arrested in the Kalachay district of Rudsar for posting content on social media. The Rudsar police commander stated that the charges are insult and public disturbance.

Masoud Pezeshkian, head of the Islamic Republic government, met with Antonio Guterres, UN Secretary-General, in New York on Friday, October 3. Before the negotiations, he signed the UN memorial book. Pezeshkian traveled to New York to attend the 81st UN General Assembly.

Shahbaz Sharif stated that Pakistan brought Washington and Tehran together for negotiations through diplomatic efforts. He discussed the Middle East crisis and its impacts on lives, economy, and shipping routes. He also condemned the Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia.

Majid Roshannejad, a political prisoner in Tehran's Great Prison, is deprived of specialized medical care due to his neurological and psychiatric illness. He is held in ward four without separation according to crime type and faces harassment. Authorities prevent his transfer to external medical centers.

Adidas unveiled a special jersey for Argentina's national football team for Lionel Messi's farewell match. Messi will wear the number 10 jersey for the last time on October 6 in a friendly match against Benin. This match marks the end of Messi's international football career.

Shida Saberi, a resident of Shiraz, was arrested by security police officers on Sunday, 29th of Shahrivar. She was transferred to Adelabad prison in Shiraz. This news was reported by HRANA news agency.

The Scottish prosecution announced that the 34-year-old Iranian man detained while attempting to enter the UK's nuclear submarine base is currently not being prosecuted. He was arrested along with a Romanian woman in March 2026. The case may be pursued if further evidence is found.

A citizen reported in a video to Iran International that GPS is down and the internet is weak on the route from Isfahan to Tehran. He says this situation makes driving very difficult. This problem is ongoing.

The Prime Minister of Qatar described the situation in the Strait of Hormuz as very difficult and challenging. He said the security of this international waterway is at risk and ship passage is problematic. He called for an end to the use of waterways for pressure and extortion.

The Court of Appeals of Qom Province confirmed the sentences of lashes and artistic activity bans for Parasto Ahmadi and eight other members involved in the Caravanserai concert. Previously, they were sentenced to 74 lashes, two years of travel ban, and two years of prohibition from artistic activities. The verdict was initially issued by the criminal court.

Nawaf Salam, the Prime Minister of Lebanon, stated at the United Nations that attacks by the Islamic Republic threaten regional security and maritime navigation. He said the consequences extend beyond conflicts, affecting supply chains, commodity prices, and inflation rates. These remarks were made on Friday, September 24.

Masoud Pezeshkian appreciated Xi Jinping's support for returning to the Islamabad agreement and resolving disputes through dialogue. He emphasized that the Islamic Republic seeks to implement agreed commitments and serious negotiations. He also noted the alignment of Tehran and Beijing's views on respecting national sovereignty and maintaining regional stability.
The audio version of Harf Akhar with Pouria Zeraati has been released. The topic covers details of the US plan to resume attacks. This was reported by Iran International.

The Tehran prosecutor's office has filed a legal case against the cast of the play "Tehran/Paris/Tehran/Bridge." This action followed the release of images from the play's performance. The images showed Fatemeh Masoudifar and Mehrdad Sedighian performing a scene.

A citizen reported that children's play equipment was removed from the park in Payam Town, Karaj. In its place, an anonymous cemetery was established. Additionally, a Hosseiniyeh for Basijis was built nearby.

The dormitory of the Zarrineh boys' boarding high school in Divandareh has been used as a military base since Esfand 1404. This has deprived students, especially those from nearby villages, of access to the dormitory. Consequently, the education of some students has been disrupted due to the difficulty of daily commuting.

Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi, during a meeting with his Indian counterpart in New York, said that Iran and Oman have negotiated an agreement to create a safe shipping route in the Strait of Hormuz. He added that he briefed the Indian foreign minister on the latest status of these talks. Araghchi also blamed US actions against Iran's commercial shipping as the main source of insecurity in the region and the Strait of Hormuz.

Kaveh Madani, head of the Water, Environment, and Health Institute at the United Nations University, described the water crisis as a new axis for global cooperation. He emphasized that the water issue has become a concern beyond developing countries, reaching Europe and North America. Madani warned that using water as a tool for political pressure could increase tensions.

Danny Danon, Israel's ambassador to the UN, said Israel desires and hopes for a regime change in Iran. He added that this is not the official goal of Israel's military operations but would benefit the people of Iran and the region. He also mentioned that regional countries like Bahrain and the UAE have taken a firm stance against the Islamic Republic.

Fereshteh Pezeshk said that both the US and Israel want to change the government in Iran but have different views on how to achieve it. She added that Israel alone cannot remove the Islamic Republic. Trump is trying to impose his demands on the Islamic Republic, but the ultimate goal of the US remains unclear.

Abbas Araghchi announced that Iran has presented a specific seven-day plan to the US for reopening the Strait of Hormuz. The final decision on this plan rests with Washington. Araghchi added that the necessary actions were previously included in the June agreement between the two countries.

The French national football team defeated Turkey in their first match under Zinedine Zidane's coaching. Kylian Mbappe scored in the 54th minute but was injured in his left knee and was substituted. France had several scoring opportunities, while Turkey also created some chances to equalize.

The Italian national football team lost 2-0 to Belgium in the first week of the UEFA Nations League. The goals were scored by Michy Batshuayi and Romelu Lukaku. After the match, a verbal altercation occurred between Gianluigi Donnarumma and Romelu Lukaku.
In the audio version 24 with Fardad Farahzad, the criticism of Lebanon and Iraq against the Islamic Republic was discussed.

The chiefs of staff of Saudi Arabia, Pakistan, and Turkey held a meeting in Riyadh emphasizing their commitment to collective defense of Saudi Arabia's security and territorial integrity. They condemned attacks on Mecca and Saudi Arabia's civilian infrastructure. They also discussed expanding intelligence and military cooperation to strengthen collective defense.

The Qom appellate court confirmed the conviction of Parasto Ahmadi and eight others involved in the Caravanserai concert. In the initial trial, these artists were sentenced to 74 lashes, two years of travel ban, and two years of prohibition from artistic activities. The appellate court's ruling remained unchanged.

Kambiz Tavana said the reaction of Iranian officials to the flight suspensions has been mostly threatening. US sanctions pressure may force regional airlines to stop cooperating with Iran. China's position remains unclear and may be influenced by recent talks between Trump and Xi Jinping.

The spokesperson of the IRGC stated that the Islamic Republic will continue to punish the US until its seven conditions are met. He said Iran's missiles can destroy the US multilayered defenses. Also, control of the Strait of Hormuz is in the hands of the IRGC Navy, and passage through the strait is now limited to oil from Iran's trading partners.

Mohammad Qaedi said China is unlikely to guarantee the implementation of any agreement between Iran and the US because Beijing-Washington relations go beyond the Iran issue. He added that until the final decision-maker in Tehran is clear, China's effective role will be difficult. Qaedi also said Iran's leverage in the Strait of Hormuz will erode over time, complicating nuclear negotiations if no agreement is reached.

Shahram Kholdi said Israel, as the only democracy in the Middle East, plays an important role in removing the Islamic Republic. He added that the disagreement between the US and Israel is about how to change the government in Iran, not the principle of change. The US prefers change from within the government, while Israel views all factions of the Islamic Republic as a single structure.
